concerns.text: The validation of model performance (macro‑F1, loss convergence) and the attribution check (ester bond in top scores for ≥90% of hydrolysis cases) are performed against synthetic degradation labels that are generated deterministically when ground‑truth is missing. Because these synthetic labels are not independent of the predictors (they are assigned without regard to molecular structure), the evaluation is circular: the model is being judged on its ability to reproduce a label distribution that was imposed arbitrarily, and the attribution validation then claims mechanistic insight based on that same synthetic labeling. This violates the independence requirement for validation targets and renders the claimed scientific conclusions non‑empirical.

The χ² test is described as being applied to "all identified motifs" to assess significance, yet the implementation (T029b) only generates a null distribution by shuffling importance scores for ester‑bond features. Applying a χ² test to continuous attribution scores (or to a subset of motifs) is a methodological mismatch and does not provide a valid test of structure‑mechanism association. Moreover, using the same model‑derived attributions both to generate the null distribution and to test significance creates a tautological validation loop.
